title: Grateful Dead Live at The Ark on 1969-04-21
lineage: SBD > MR > DAT > CDA > DAW(Bertha) > CDA/SHN

ai_review.summary: Stellar soundboard capture of a high‑energy 1969 show with superb Viola Lee Blues, Dark Star/Eleven/Lovelight runs and excellent mix despite minor tape quirks
ai_review.review: The recording is an SBD (soundboard) master that delivers crystal‑clear instrument separation, only marred by occasional hiss, a few cut‑outs and a missing three‑minute Foxy Lady jam segment. Musically the concert is a showcase of the band's late‑spring ’69 fire – Viola Lee Blues, Dark Star into St Stephen, The Eleven and Turn On Your Lovelight are repeatedly praised as peak performances, while the first set is viewed as uneven with an all‑igator version that many deem weak.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 30 reviews overwhelmingly rate the show 4–5 stars, highlighting both exceptional performance and high‑quality soundboard mix; only a few isolated negatives keep the average below 4½.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear, balanced SBD mix with rich bass response; minor hiss and occasional reel‑end cut‑out noted, plus a missing 3‑4 min Foxy Lady jam segment.

standout_songs: Dark Star > St. Stephen > The Eleven > Turn On Your Lovelight
Hard To Handle (noted for slide work)
Foxy Lady jam (polarizing but often praised)
poor_songs: Hard To Handle (mixed opinions on execution)
Foxy Lady jam (some reviewers think it sloppy)
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set is uneven – solid moments but a few weak renditions – while the second set erupts with fire, delivering classic long jams and seamless transitions that lift the overall energy.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Rich, fuzzy tone praised; shredding solos on Viola Lee Blues and The Other One; slide guitar experiment on Hard To Handle noted (mixed reception).
band_member_comments.Phil: "Phil is HUGE" – bass highlighted for power, visceral response, and “bombs” during The Eleven.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill and Mickey’s duet described as solid groove; drum work on St. Stephen likened to firecrackers.
